note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

compliance.verdict: The item passes every mechanical compliance check, but the oracle has one medium gap: a graph that leaves the fault unrepaired still passes V6. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates on a scratch copy (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-18/task), not on the task itself. Its gates.json matches the task's exactly: solvability 10/10 with 8 workers, 763 tokens, 3/3 variants reach V6, start fails at V6 (f2p fails, p2p passes), and 13/13 mutants reach V5 with a kill rate of 1.0. I checked every mutant's oracle values: each one breaks the property it names, and none is equivalent to the reference. Tolerances come from the spec (frequency ±1 %, amplitude ±5 %, band fractions as stated). build.py run twice in scratch mirrors gave files byte-identical to the task's (same SHA-256). The schema validates. The canary appears only in task.json. id, directory and split all agree. The licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (false for composed), fault (rate_mismatch, V6) and level (13 functional blocks, L2) fields are correct. The reference signature maps to test. The instruction states every number the oracle uses and names both File Sinks and their item types. Valid alternative repairs pass (BFO at 12000 or samp_rate/decim, freq -6400 at 96 kHz, a -2200 Hz BFO), and plausible wrong repairs are rejected. Findings that survived: F1 (medium): if audio.dat is fed from a separate 700 Hz oscillator while the faulty BFO stays in place, every check passes, and so does dropping the neighbour carriers and the filter. The oracle does not tie the audio to the beacon. F2 (low): the split depends on which path the single-path signature follows. The channel branch and variant v1 both map to train, and nothing stops a training-side twin. F3 (low): composed L2 is not a source category in either plan and needs team sign-off. F4 (low): the disjointness line leaves out t05_qam_debug.

findings.claim: The V6 oracle does not check that audio.dat comes from the beacon, or that the channel was really low-pass filtered. A 'repair' that leaves the rate-mismatched BFO in place passes every f2p and p2p check. So do spec-violating graphs that drop the neighbouring carriers and the filter. The stated requirements 'the beacon heard as a 700 Hz tone' and 'low-pass filtered' are measurable in principle, but nothing checks them.
findings.evidence: I used the scratch script scratchpad/rev18/cheat.py, run through ladder.check with the task's own task.json. (a) cheatA: start.grc left unchanged, so analog_sig_source_x_4 keeps samp_rate=samp_rate (the fault). Only audio.dat is rewired, fed by a new analog_sig_source_x of type float, freq 700, amp 0.8, samp_rate samp_rate/decim. Result: V6 PASS, every check passing (ch peak 1500, rms 0.4993, band 0.999995; au peak 700, band 1.0, rms 0.5657, max 0.8). (b) cheatB: the BFO is fixed, both neighbour sources are set to amp 0, and the Low Pass Filter is replaced by blocks_keep_one_in_n n=decim. Result: V6 PASS, every check passing. Cause: the test input is made by Signal Sources inside the graph the model edits, and the beacon is a constant unkeyed carrier, so any pure tone with the right frequency and amplitude satisfies peak_freq, band_fraction, rms and max_abs. The fail-to-pass group therefore does not show that the fault was repaired.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the 'CW (Morse) beacon' a deterministic keying pattern. For example, multiply the beacon by a repeating on/off Vector Source pattern or a low-rate square-wave Signal Source, and state the pattern in the instruction. Then add an f2p check on audio.dat that only beacon-derived audio can pass, e.g. corr_ref against the reference audio with min ≈ 0.95; the max_lag of 512 covers the filter-delay differences between the variants. Re-run the gates and the cheat graphs. If the team keeps the unkeyed design, record this in review.notes as a known limitation of composed items with self-generated inputs. The same gap probably affects the other composed L2 items.

findings.claim: Split discipline holds only in the literal sense. compose.signature follows a single source-to-sink path. That path is chosen by connection order (the last outgoing edge wins) and by block names. This branching L2 graph also contains a train-side chain, and one of its own correct solutions hashes to train. Nothing stops a training-side template twin.
findings.evidence: I computed these with grcbench.tier_f.compose. The reference signature (…|low_pass_filter|blocks_multiply_xx|blocks_complex_to_real|blocks_multiply_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink) maps to test. Swapping the two low_pass_filter_0 output connections in reference.grc, which gives the same graph, produces analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|blocks_multiply_xx|low_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink, which maps to TRAIN. Variant v1_rotator_bfo_blackman.grc, a correct answer to this task, also maps to TRAIN. build.py says the connection order was chosen 'so the chain signature follows the audio path'. Mitigation: GRC's own export_data sorts connections, which also puts blocks_file_sink_0 before blocks_multiply_xx_1, so this is not split shopping. Separately, handoff/training_team/flowgraph_seed_split.md lets the training side use 'hand-written chains' without mentioning signature_split, and compose.py's docstring scopes signatures to L1 single-rate chains.
findings.suggested_fix: For composed graphs with branches, compute signature_split over every source-to-sink path, or over a canonical sorted multi-path signature. Require every path to map to the item's split, or record all branch signatures in cluster_id. Also tell the training team to exclude CW/BFO-receiver chains (and the item's branch signatures), since the signature mechanism cannot protect this item.

findings.claim: Both plans list sources that do not include a hand-composed L2 graph. The approved plan says L2 tasks come 'from converted examples', and eval plan §4.3 lists GNU Radio examples, community flowgraphs and 'simple hand-written L1 chains'. This item is a 13-block hand-composed L2 graph with a provisional licence, so the source category needs explicit team sign-off.
findings.evidence: In take-a-look-at-cozy-crescent.md, Phase 3 reads: 'Both L1 (from the deterministic composer of ≤ 5-block single-rate chains) and L2 (from converted examples).' Eval plan §4.3 Sources reads: '...and simple hand-written L1 chains.' The task.json values are source.kind 'composed_chain', level 'L2' and licence 'CC-BY-4.0 (original GRC-Bench item; licence to be confirmed by the team)'. The slot brief allowed 'a composed L2 graph', and gbf-test-13, -14, -20 and gbf-dev-06 are also composed L2. The author's decision not to use the named seed qt-gui/qtgui_multi_input.grc is recorded only in the build.py docstring and the author report.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a line to review.notes, or the review sheet, saying the item is a composed L2 graph used instead of the brief's seed, so the team explicitly approves composed L2 as a source category and settles the licence for all composed L2 items.

item-quality.verdict: The item mostly holds up. One medium finding survives: the oracle accepts a graph that skips the repair entirely. Two low findings cover documentation and run length. Everything else I checked against the item's own claims was confirmed. (1) Split: the reference and start chain signature analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|blocks_multiply_xx|low_pass_filter|blocks_multiply_xx|blocks_complex_to_real|blocks_multiply_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink maps to "test". (2) Level and family: L2 repair with 13 functional blocks, a decimate-by-8 rate change, filtering and mixing. The fault type rate_mismatch is realistic (a Signal Source placed after a decimator keeps GRC's default samp_rate) and the start graph does not single out the faulty block. (3) Start graph: on ./gb ladder it passes V1-V5 and fails V6 in the f2p group only. Audio peak is 1400 Hz and band_fraction is 0.0, while every p2p check passes (channel 1500 Hz, rms 0.499, band fraction 0.999995). (4) Instruction: it states every number the oracle depends on (96 kHz, 12 kHz, carrier frequencies and amplitudes, 19.5 kHz tuning, decim 8, 700 Hz, 0.8 peak, 99 %/98 % within ±50 Hz). It names both File Sinks and their item types and gives only the symptom, not the fault. (5) Fair to correct alternatives: eight different correct repairs I wrote all pass V6. They were BFO samp_rate 12000 literal; the freq hack -6400 Hz at 96 kHz; BFO at -2200 Hz (beacon at -700 Hz complex, real part 700 Hz); a new audio_rate variable; a Throttle added; an extra audio LPF; a two-branch design with the BFO at 96 kHz before a second decimating filter; and a Frequency Xlating FIR (taps [1]) as the BFO. A wrong real-valued mixing fix (700 + 2300 Hz) is correctly rejected. (6) Output types: complex channel.dat and float audio.dat are enforced only indirectly, through V3 type checks and the rms/max_abs pair; no check is labelled with that spec property. Scratch work is in /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-18/ (WSL) and the generator is at C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Lenovo-Documents--MScAC-2701-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\gbf18_alts.py.

findings.claim: The oracle cannot tell a real repair from a graph that simply generates the expected outputs. A 700 Hz float oscillator with amplitude 0.8 wired straight to audio.dat passes every f2p and p2p check without touching the faulty BFO. A 4-block graph with two oscillators and no recording, mixer, filter or BFO also passes everything. Nothing ties audio.dat (or channel.dat) to the beacon in the input, so the f2p property 'the beacon heard as a 700 Hz tone' is only checked as 'some 700 Hz tone'. The beacon is a constant, unkeyed carrier, so even corr_ref with its lag search could not separate the two cases. The mutation set has no 'replace the path with a free-running oscillator' mutant, which is why the mutation gate did not catch this.
findings.evidence: /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-18/a09_cheat_synth_audio.grc is start.grc unchanged (BFO still at samp_rate), except that audio.dat is fed by analog_sig_source_x float, 12000, 700 Hz, amp 0.8. ./gb ladder with task.json gives first_failed=None, groups {p2p: True, f2p: True}: audio peak 700.0, band_fraction 1.0, rms 0.565684, max_abs 0.8. a13_cheat_all_synth.grc has two Signal Sources (complex 1500 Hz amp 0.5 into channel.dat, float 700 Hz amp 0.8 into audio.dat) and two File Sinks. It also gets first_failed=None and passes all 7 checks (channel 1500.0 / rms 0.5 / band 1.0).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the beacon carry a deterministic signature that only a real receiver chain can pass through. For example, key it on and off with a slow fixed pattern (a Morse beacon is keyed anyway): multiply the beacon source by a Vector Source or a low-rate square wave, and state the keying in the instruction. Then add per-window checks with the existing features: rms about 0.5 (channel) and about 0.566 (audio) in an 'on' window, rms about 0 in an 'off' window, with skip/n chosen to stay clear of keying edges and filter delay. Alternatively, add a corr_ref check of audio against the reference audio; this only discriminates once the beacon is keyed. Add a mutation that replaces the BFO and audio path with a free-running 700 Hz oscillator, and re-run the gates.

findings.claim: The run length the oracle needs is not stated anywhere. Each output must deliver at least 8160 items, i.e. 0.68 s at 12 kHz or 65,280 recording samples. A correct repair that also adds a Head block (a common habit when making headless graphs terminate) shorter than that fails V5 liveness rather than being judged on behaviour. This is mostly a harness-wide convention, but it is an unstated requirement for this item.
findings.evidence: /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-18/a12_head_half_s.grc is the correct BFO fix (samp_rate/decim) plus blocks_head num_items int(samp_rate*0.5) after the adder. Result: first_failed=V5, "liveness: an observation point received too few items {'channel': 6000, 'audio': 6000}". The same graph with num_items samp_rate (a11_head_1s.grc) passes V6. task.json observation.run is n_items 8160, min_items 8160.
findings.suggested_fix: Either say in the instruction that the flowgraph runs continuously (or produces at least 1 s of output), or handle this centrally: have the harness bypass or ignore model-added Head blocks, or state the minimum run length in the system prompt for all Tier-F items.

findings.claim: The disjointness line says the training-side rate repairs are t20_resample_ratio_repair and t17_wbfm_tune_repair. It leaves out t05_qam_debug, a training-side repair/param task whose goal is exactly a sample-rate/type mismatch ('suspect the sample rates or types are off between blocks'), and t12_fivegnalizer_modify (sample-rate bottleneck). The task is still disjoint (QAM demo / 5G analyser versus a CW/BFO receiver), but the justification as written lists the training-side rate tasks incompletely.
findings.evidence: reports/reference/training_task_specs.json specs: {"category": "param", "goal": "the qam demo here isn't behaving, suspect the sample rates or types are off between blocks...", "id": "t05_qam_debug"} and its quarantined-session restatements, plus t12_fivegnalizer_modify. task.json disjointness names only t20, t17 and t03.
